## Natural history notes

A stocky, medium-sized kingfisher characterized by a large head, shaggy crest, long dagger-like bill, blue-gray upperparts, white collar, and a broad blue breast band, with females also showing a rusty belly band. In Florida, the Belted Kingfisher is found along rivers, lakes, ponds, canals, marshes, mangroves, estuaries, and coastal shorelines, especially where clear water and exposed perches are available. It hunts by watching from branches, wires, docks, or posts and plunging into the water for small fish, crayfish, tadpoles, and aquatic insects, and it nests in burrows dug into sandy or earthen banks.
